chunks: Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from Ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ibn Bashir, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Hamza who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: My father (peace be upon him) said:

Verily Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya was a man with a fearless heart – and he pointed with his hand – and he was making Tawaf around the House when Hajjaj encountered him. He said: I desired to strike that which holds your eyes [i.e. cut off your head]! Muhammad said to him: Never! Verily Allah – Blessed is His Name – has three hundred moments each day over His creatures, perhaps one of them can get rid of you for me.
ai.seo_question: What did Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya say to Hajjaj when threatened with death?
ai.summary: This narration highlights the composure (rabt al-ja'sh) of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya, a key figure in early Shia political theology, during his confrontation with the Umayyad governor Hajjaj ibn Yusuf. The reference to 'three hundred moments' (al-lahat) reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of divine omnipresence and the immediacy of Allah's decree, offering a theological counter to human power. It underscores the concept of divine protection (tawfiq) for the righteous even amidst political oppression.
